newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude - Summer demand drives heavy crudes.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - Summer demand drives heavy crudes.

text.p: Prices of Asia's heavy crudes continued to climb on Japan's utility demand, while China is buying up the last of the July barrels, traders said on Tuesday.
A 50,000-barrel parcel of July Minas was sold by an equity producer at ICP +50/55 cents per barrel to Japan.
But rumours that an August Minas trade was also done by an equity producer at ICP +50/60 could not be confirmed.
China was heard to have bought two parcels of July Widuri, each of 200,000 barrels, from a producer at ICP +25 and ICP +30.
There was limited discussion on the Asian light crudes for August.
But a partial cargo of Kutubu loading at the end of July was sold to an Australian refiner, around Tapis APPI -35 cents cost and freight (c+f).
Some traders said this would netback to APPI -$1.35 free-on-board (fob). This was disputed by others, who assessed the freight costs lower than $1.00.
The seller had offered a full cargo, but the remaining barrels were heard going into its own system in Australia.
The outlook for light grades in August is less bearish as supplies tighten, but levels are unlikely to go higher than APPI -80/90 for Cossack and Kutubu, traders said.
In the Mideast crude market, Oman trading was thin, with two cargoes and three partials heard still available for August.
But with buying interest heard coming from China, levels are not expected to fall much lower than recent deals.
August Oman was last done at Dubai -3, traders said.
A south Korean refiner heard bought 200,000 barrels of August Qatar Land from a European major at Dubai +32/33.
The European major also heard selling 200,000 barrels of Qatar land to a Japanese refiner, in exchange for the same volume of Murban.
